diagnostics.message: `google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment` takes `policy_id` straight from `var.firewall_policy_attachments` (a plain string), while the hierarchical firewall policies it attaches are created in this same module by `google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy`. Because there is no attribute reference or `depends_on` between them, Terraform can create/associate the policy before the policy exists on a first apply (the provider's own example sets `policy_id = google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy.id`). The association should be ordered after the security policy — e.g. `policy_id = try(google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy[each.key].id, each.value)` so a module-created policy is referenced when the attachment key matches a policy key and externally supplied IDs still win otherwise, or a bare `depends_on = [google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy]`.
